pipeline_components.name: Camera input
pipeline_components.detail: SANPO (primary, dense depth) or AEA (secondary, sparse depth) recorded sequences, replayed frame-by-frame -- not a live feed. See PROJECT_PLAN.md's demo section for why replay was chosen over live camera.

pipeline_components.name: Muse Spark / Meta Model API
pipeline_components.detail: Proposes which object concepts to track from the first frame of a sequence. OpenAI-SDK-compatible client against api.meta.ai/v1.

pipeline_components.name: SAM 3.1 Object Multiplex
pipeline_components.detail: One video session per concept (native API constraint, not a design choice -- no multi-concept single pass). use_fa3=False.
pipeline_components.known_limitation: scripts/smoke_test_sam31.py (per-session throughput with 4-6 concurrent concept sessions) is not yet filled in.

pipeline_components.name: Median-depth mask lifting
pipeline_components.detail: lift() takes the median depth under a segmentation mask; lift_from_box() (condition C only) takes the median depth under the detection's bounding box instead.

pipeline_components.name: Persistent world-memory graph
pipeline_components.detail: SpatialMemoryGraph: temporal decay, eviction, spatial re-association, periodic duplicate-node merging (found and fixed on real SAM 3.1 output -- see docs/CLAUDE.md).

pipeline_components.name: Geometric TTC
pipeline_components.detail: distance / closing speed, computed directly in geometry/kinematics.py. No learned model (explicitly not a GATv2/GNN).

pipeline_components.name: SeamlessM4T v2
pipeline_components.detail: Real open Meta speech model via transformers. Voicebox/Audiobox were investigated and found not publicly available.

pipeline_components.name: Ray-Ban Display output
pipeline_components.detail: No physical Ray-Ban Display hardware connected; HUD preview renders the same directive/tone data a real device would receive, clearly labelled as a preview, not a live hardware feed.

frames.camera_frame: F_ego -- OpenCV convention, +Z forward, +X right, +Y down.
frames.body_frame: F_body -- torso/clock-face frame, +Z = direction of travel from smoothed world-frame velocity, independent of head orientation.
frames.world_frame: F_world -- fixed world coordinates from each dataset's own pose source (AEA: MPS SLAM trajectory; SANPO: fixed_camera_poses.csv).
frames.invariant_tested: A static object's body-frame bearing stays constant under pure camera rotation -- tested directly in tests/test_geometry.py.

transform_consistency_check.what: Cross-validated the velocity-derived body-frame heading (core design assumption behind the whole clock-face/body split) against SANPO's literal, independently-measured chest-camera orientation -- the first time this project checked the body-frame approximation against anything other than 'it seems reasonable'.
transform_consistency_check.result_note: Larger excursions occur during turns, where a velocity-smoothed estimate legitimately lags real-time orientation. This is a median-level agreement with real scatter, not an exact match.
bugs_found_by_this_check: Camera intrinsics mixup: description.json's session_camera_details[0] was used unconditionally regardless of requested camera -- silently wrong for camera_chest. Fixed by selecting on `model` name, cross-verified against each camera's documented stereo baseline.

SANPO's local-forward axis is not OpenCV's +Z, unlike AEA. Found via systematic testing of all 6 candidate signed local axes against real velocity data -- local -X gives a clean ~22deg median residual, every other axis gives 100+ degrees of uncorrelated error.
transform_consistency_check.unresolved_caveat: The up/right axes of SANPO's local rotation convention remain a genuinely open question: the dataset's own feature name (camera_quaternions_right_handed_y_up) implies translation Y is vertical, but the loader's own fixed_camera_poses.csv shows Z is the bounded (vertical-gait-bob) axis and Y is the dominant walking axis -- the opposite of what the name implies. This affects only lateral/vertical placement of lifted 3D points, not depth-along-ray or heading, which is why the heading validation above still holds despite this being unresolved. Full writeup: src/locus/data/sanpo_loader.py module docstring.

latency_disclaimer: No per-stage wall-clock instrumentation exists in the production pipeline (scripts/generate_dashboard_data.py, scripts/run_real_sequence.py). Any latency figure shown for the real pipeline stages (Spark/SAM 3.1/TTS) would be fabricated -- the System page must mark per-stage latency as 'not measured' rather than show a number. The only real timing data in this repo is the synthetic eval harness's relative per-condition wall-clock comparison in dashboard/data/ablation_results.json, which explicitly is not a deployed-system latency benchmark.
